title: Second best

idea.rule: sorted() hands you a NEW list — the old one stays exactly as it was.
idea.detail: sorted(scores) returns a fresh list in order and leaves scores untouched — but here the returned list is never caught: it is built, then thrown away. scores still sits in shelf order. If you read [-2] off scores, you're reading the unsorted order: the second-to-last score on the shelf, not the second-best score. Catch the sorted list and read the answer off it.

model_restatement: Sort the scores, take the second-best one, and print it.

clarify.question: What if two scores tie for second-best?
What if there are only two scores?
clarify.answer: Then the lower one is second-best.

clarify.question: Can I change the order of the list?
clarify.answer: Yes — sorting a copy leaves the original alone.

clarify.question: What if there are no scores?
clarify.answer: Today there are always at least two scores.

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Sort the scores, take the second-to-last one from the scores, and announce it.

checkpoints.prompt: With the fix — after line 2, what is second?

why_line: scores[-2] reads the ORIGINAL list — still in shelf order [42, 87, 65] — so the second-to-last score on the shelf is 87, the best, not the second-best.

explain.rule: sorted() hands you a new list in order — but second is read off scores, which never moved: [-2] of the shelf order is 87.
explain.bridge: After line 1, where did the sorted list go — and which list does line 2 read?

fix.rule: Read [-2] off ordered: the sorted copy's second-to-last is the second-best score.

walk.gloss: Catch the sorted list in ordered — scores itself stays in shelf order.
Take the second-to-last of the SORTED copy.

contrast.right_note: caught — read the answer off it

alternatives.note: Sort in place instead — then the original IS the sorted list.
